input.text:
You are the perception stage of a physics simulator for robotics teams.
The video is a short side-view clip from a static camera. Image A is its first frame, image B its last frame.
List the rigid objects that move (or are about to move) and any large static objects they could hit.
Approximate each object as a circle or a box and estimate its real size in cm from everyday knowledge
(e.g. tennis ball ~6.7 cm). Give the support surfaces as line segments along their top edges.
Estimate each object's mass in grams, and say whether each support surface is hard or soft.
Classify the main object's motion. Bounding boxes and lines use [y, x] order normalized to 0-1000.

name.description: short noun phrase, e.g. 'grey tennis ball'
name.title: Name

est_real_size_cm.description: real-world diameter (circle) or width (box) in cm
est_real_size_cm.title: Est Real Size Cm

moving.description: true if this object moves at any time in the clip
moving.title: Moving

bbox_frame0.description: [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] normalized 0-1000 in the FIRST frame; [0,0,0,0] if not visible
bbox_frame0.title: Bbox Frame0

bbox_last_frame.description: [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] normalized 0-1000 in the LAST frame; [0,0,0,0] if not visible
bbox_last_frame.title: Bbox Last Frame

est_mass_g.description: estimated real mass in grams from everyday knowledge (e.g. coffee mug ~300, brick ~2000)
est_mass_g.title: Est Mass G

line.description: top edge the object rests/rolls on, as [y1, x1, y2, x2] normalized 0-1000 in the last frame
line.title: Line

material.description: soft: objects sink in and stop (bedding, cushions, foam, sand); hard: they bounce or roll (wood, stone, plastic, glass)
material.title: Material

motion_start_s.description: time in seconds when the main object starts moving (or appears)
motion_start_s.title: Motion Start S

input.text:
You are the perception stage of a physics simulator for robotics teams.
The video is a short side-view clip from a static camera. Image A is its first frame, image B its last frame.
List the rigid objects that move (or are about to move) and any large static objects they could hit.
Approximate each object as a circle or a box and estimate its real size in cm from everyday knowledge
(e.g. tennis ball ~6.7 cm). Give the support surfaces as line segments along their top edges.
Estimate each object's mass in grams, and say whether each support surface is hard or soft.
Classify the main object's motion. Bounding boxes and lines use [y, x] order normalized to 0-1000.

name.description: short noun phrase, e.g. 'grey tennis ball'
name.title: Name

est_real_size_cm.description: real-world diameter (circle) or width (box) in cm
est_real_size_cm.title: Est Real Size Cm

moving.description: true if this object moves at any time in the clip
moving.title: Moving

bbox_frame0.description: [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] normalized 0-1000 in the FIRST frame; [0,0,0,0] if not visible
bbox_frame0.title: Bbox Frame0

bbox_last_frame.description: [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] normalized 0-1000 in the LAST frame; [0,0,0,0] if not visible
bbox_last_frame.title: Bbox Last Frame

est_mass_g.description: estimated real mass in grams from everyday knowledge (e.g. coffee mug ~300, brick ~2000)
est_mass_g.title: Est Mass G

line.description: top edge the object rests/rolls on, as [y1, x1, y2, x2] normalized 0-1000 in the last frame
line.title: Line

material.description: soft: objects sink in and stop (bedding, cushions, foam, sand); hard: they bounce or roll (wood, stone, plastic, glass)
material.title: Material

motion_start_s.description: time in seconds when the main object starts moving (or appears)
motion_start_s.title: Motion Start S

You are the perception stage of a physics simulator for robotics teams.
The video is a short side-view clip from a static camera. Image A is its first frame, image B its last frame.
List the rigid objects that move (or are about to move) and any large static objects they could hit.
Approximate each object as a circle or a box and estimate its real size in cm from everyday knowledge
(e.g. tennis ball ~6.7 cm). Give the support surfaces as line segments along their top edges.
Estimate each object's mass in grams, and say whether each support surface is hard or soft.
Classify the main object's motion. Bounding boxes and lines use [y, x] order normalized to 0-1000.

material.description: soft: objects sink in and stop (bedding, cushions, foam, sand); hard: they bounce or roll (wood, stone, plastic, glass)

line.description: top edge the object rests/rolls on, as [y1, x1, y2, x2] normalized 0-1000 in the last frame

material.description: soft: objects sink in and stop (bedding, cushions, foam, sand); hard: they bounce or roll (wood, stone, plastic, glass)
